components.note: 又 (hand) — two hands 又 stacked: hands joined in friendship.

example.hanzi: 他是我最好的朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyou.
example.english: He is my best friend.
example.fact: 友 is bound: 朋友 (friend), 友好 (friendly), 友谊 (friendship), 校友 (alumnus), 室友 (roommate), and 网友 (online friend). The old picture is two hands clasped, an apt image for friendship.

examples.hanzi: 我和邻居成了好朋友。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé línjū chéng le hǎo péngyou.
examples.english: My neighbor and I became good friends.

examples.hanzi: 周末我要去见一位老友。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ yào qù jiàn yí wèi lǎoyǒu.
examples.english: This weekend I am going to see an old friend.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
朋 (friend) — oldest form shows two strings of cowrie shells (old money) side by side; they paired up and came to mean companions.
又 (hand) — two hands 又 stacked: hands joined in friendship.

example.hanzi: 公园里有很多小朋友在玩耍。
example.pinyin: gōngyuán lǐ yǒu hěnduō xiǎopéngyǒu zài wánshuǎ.
example.english: There are many children playing in the park.
example.fact: Children's brains reach about 90% of their adult size by age five, but the prefrontal cortex — responsible for judgment and impulse control — continues developing until the mid-20s. That's part of why risk assessment and decision-making mature so much later than overall brain size.

examples.hanzi: 小朋友，请排好队。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎopéngyou, qǐng pái hǎo duì.
examples.english: Kids, please line up.

examples.hanzi: 幼儿园的小朋友在唱歌。
examples.pinyin: Yòu'éryuán de xiǎopéngyou zài chànggē.
examples.english: The kindergarten kids are singing.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and pouring, as in 河, 海, 清: 注 is to pour in.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; 主 also in 住 zhù, 柱 zhù and 驻 zhù.
册 — bamboo slips bound with a cord, the ancient book; today a volume or register, as in 手册 manual, 注册 register.

example.hanzi: 新生需要在开学前完成网上注册。
example.pinyin: xīnshēng xūyào zài kāixué qián wánchéng wǎngshàng zhùcè.
example.english: New students need to complete online registration before the semester starts.
example.fact: The first-ever registered .com domain name, symbolics.com, was registered on March 15, 1985, by a now-defunct computer company. It predates the World Wide Web itself by six years and is preserved today as a piece of internet history rather than used commercially.

examples.hanzi: 请先注册一个账号再登录。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiān zhùcè yí ge zhànghào zài dēnglù.
examples.english: Please register an account before logging in.

examples.hanzi: 你注册了这门课吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhùcè le zhè mén kè ma?
examples.english: Have you enrolled in this course?

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and meeting, as in 过, 进, 送; 遭 is to meet, usually with bad luck.
曹 (cáo) hints at the sound: 遭 zāo is close to 糟 zāo and 槽 cáo.
又 (hand) — two hands pass a vessel: one gives, one receives; 授 shòu adds 扌 for "give".

example.hanzi: 这座城市遭受了严重的洪灾。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò chéngshì zāoshòule yánzhòng de hóngzāi.
example.english: This city suffered severe flood damage.
example.fact: The 1931 China floods along the Yangtze and Huai rivers are considered by many historians to be the deadliest natural disaster ever recorded, with death toll estimates ranging from several hundred thousand to over 4 million once the resulting famine and disease are factored in.

examples.hanzi: 这个村子遭受了严重的干旱。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cūnzi zāoshòu le yánzhòng de gānhàn.
examples.english: This village suffered a severe drought.

examples.hanzi: 他在比赛中遭受了失败。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng zāoshòu le shībài.
examples.english: He suffered a defeat in the competition.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — a body-part radical, as in 脸 face, 脚 foot, 胖 fat; 肿 is flesh swelling.
中 (zhōng) gives a close sound, with a different tone; 种 zhǒng shares the same pair.
疒 (illness) — marks diseases and ailments, as in 病 sick, 痛 pain; 瘤 is a growth.
留 (liú) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 溜 liū and 榴 liú.

example.hanzi: 医生通过检查发现了一个良性肿瘤。
example.pinyin: yīshēng tōngguò jiǎnchá fāxiànle yī gè liángxìng zhǒngliú.
example.english: The doctor discovered a benign tumor through an examination.
example.fact: Tumors aren't unique to humans — paleontologists have identified likely cancerous growths in fossilized dinosaur bones dating back over 70 million years, including a probable case of osteosarcoma found in a Centrosaurus fibula described in a 2020 study.

examples.hanzi: 检查结果显示，那只是一个小肿瘤。
examples.pinyin: Jiǎnchá jiéguǒ xiǎnshì, nà zhǐshì yí ge xiǎo zhǒngliú.
examples.english: The results showed it was only a small tumor.

examples.hanzi: 医生建议尽早切除肿瘤。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì jǐnzǎo qiēchú zhǒngliú.
examples.english: The doctor advised removing the tumor as early as possible.

components.note: 气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.
口 (mouth) — tasting and speaking: 吃, 喝, 嗅; 味 is flavor.
未 (wèi) sounds exactly like 味; also 妹 mèi.

example.hanzi: 厨房里飘出一阵诱人的气味。
example.pinyin: chúfáng lǐ piāo chū yī zhèn yòurén de qìwèi.
example.english: An enticing smell drifted out from the kitchen.
example.fact: A 2014 study published in Science found that the human nose can distinguish over one trillion different odors — far more than the roughly 10,000 estimate long assumed in earlier textbooks, revealing that human olfaction is far more powerful than commonly believed.

examples.hanzi: 这朵花的气味很特别。
examples.pinyin: Zhè duǒ huā de qìwèi hěn tèbié.
examples.english: This flower has a very special scent.

examples.hanzi: 房间里有一股烟的气味。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ yǒu yì gǔ yān de qìwèi.
examples.english: There is a smell of smoke in the room.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.
聲 (traditional) — a hanging stone chime struck, with 耳 (ear) below: a sound you hear. 声 keeps only the top, so the picture is mostly lost.
士 (scholar) — the top of 声 is only a leftover of the old chime, not 'scholar'. Do not read meaning into it.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的名声很好,总是排长队。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de míngshēng hěn hǎo, zǒngshì pái chángduì.
example.english: This restaurant has a great reputation and there's always a long line.
example.fact: The Michelin Guide, now the world's most influential restaurant rating system, began in 1900 as a free booklet handed out by a French tire company to encourage more people to drive — and therefore wear out more tires. Its star ratings only became a serious culinary benchmark decades later.

examples.hanzi: 他靠诚实赢得了好名声。
examples.pinyin: Tā kào chéngshí yíngdé le hǎo míngshēng.
examples.english: He earned a good reputation through honesty.

examples.hanzi: 这位医生在当地很有名声。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yīshēng zài dāngdì hěn yǒu míngshēng.
examples.english: This doctor has a great reputation locally.

meanings: variant of 發布|发布[fa1 bu4]

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
巾 (cloth) — 巾 is a cloth radical, as in 帽 hat, 带 belt; 布 is cloth, and by extension to spread or announce, as in 宣布.

example.hanzi: 公司明天将发布新产品。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī míngtiān jiāng fābù xīn chǎnpǐn.
example.english: The company will release a new product tomorrow.
example.fact: The first iPhone was announced in January 2007, but Apple had not yet finalized the software — engineers were still working out crashes and dropped calls in the weeks leading up to Steve Jobs's live demo, carefully routing his path across the stage to avoid the spots with the weakest signal.

examples.hanzi: 学校今天发布了新的通知。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào jīntiān fābù le xīn de tōngzhī.
examples.english: The school issued a new notice today.

examples.hanzi: 这款手机什么时候发布？
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn shǒujī shénme shíhou fābù?
examples.english: When will this phone be released?

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and flowers: 花, 草, 茶; 英 first meant a flower, then outstanding, then hero.
央 (yāng) is a loose sound hint (-ng); also in 映 yìng and 殃 yāng.
亻 (person) — a good-looking person; also in 他 he, 优 excellent.
夋 (qūn) is a loose clue; it starts the jùn series 骏 jùn, 峻 jùn, 竣 jùn.

example.hanzi: 他长得很英俊,吸引了很多人的目光。
example.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de hěn yīngjùn, xīyǐn le hěn duō rén de mùguāng.
example.english: He is very handsome and attracts a lot of attention.
example.fact: Facial symmetry is one of the most consistent cross-cultural predictors of how attractive a face is judged to be, because it can signal developmental stability and the absence of disease or injury during growth. Studies using digitally averaged, symmetrical composite faces find they are rated as more appealing than almost any individual face used to build them.

examples.hanzi: 他不但英俊，而且很有礼貌。
examples.pinyin: Tā búdàn yīngjùn, érqiě hěn yǒu lǐmào.
examples.english: He is not only handsome but also very polite.

examples.hanzi: 那位英俊的演员走进了餐厅。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi yīngjùn de yǎnyuán zǒujìn le cāntīng.
examples.english: That handsome actor walked into the restaurant.

components.note: 工 (work) — a carpenter's tool shape: work, craftsman. 工 is a sound series: 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 功 gōng, 空 kōng.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 字: a room under the roof.
至 (zhì, arrive) is a loose sound clue for shì; it fits the meaning: where one arrives inside the house.

example.hanzi: 她在这个工作室里画了很多油画。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhège gōngzuòshì lǐ huà le hěn duō yóuhuà.
example.english: She has painted many oil paintings in this studio.
example.fact: Claude Monet's studio garden at Giverny, with its water lily pond and Japanese footbridge, was designed and planted by Monet himself specifically to serve as a living subject — he painted the pond in roughly 250 canvases over the last three decades of his life, watching it change with the light and seasons.

examples.hanzi: 我们的工作室周末也开门。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de gōngzuòshì zhōumò yě kāimén.
examples.english: Our studio is open on weekends too.

examples.hanzi: 他在音乐工作室录了一首新歌。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yīnyuè gōngzuòshì lù le yì shǒu xīn gē.
examples.english: He recorded a new song at a music studio.

components.note: 木 — a tree with trunk, branches and roots; the wood radical, as in 林 forest, 树 tree, 桌 table.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 工人用木头做了一张桌子。
example.pinyin: Gōngrén yòng mùtou zuò le yī zhāng zhuōzi.
example.english: The worker made a table out of wood.
example.fact: The tallest trees on Earth, coast redwoods, can grow taller than 115 meters and live for over 2,000 years, yet they have surprisingly shallow root systems — often only 3 to 4 meters deep. They survive storms by spreading their roots wide and intertwining them with neighboring trees for mutual support.

examples.hanzi: 这块木头太重了，我搬不动。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài mùtou tài zhòng le, wǒ bān bu dòng.
examples.english: This piece of wood is too heavy, and I can't move it.

examples.hanzi: 别像木头一样站着，快来帮忙！
examples.pinyin: Bié xiàng mùtou yíyàng zhànzhe, kuài lái bāngmáng!
examples.english: Don't just stand there like a block of wood, come and help!

components.note: 页 (head, page) — marks the head and face, as in 顶, 题, 顺; 预 is thinking ahead.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 预 yù is close, as in 豫 yù.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔 pen, 等 wait, 第: counting rods were once bamboo.
具 (jù, tool) — here the lower part shows hands holding the counting tools.

example.hanzi: 这次旅行的预算是五千元。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì lǔxíng de yùsuàn shì wǔqiān yuán.
example.english: The budget for this trip is five thousand yuan.
example.fact: NASA's original budget estimate for the Apollo program in 1961 was around $7 billion, but by the time of the first Moon landing in 1969 total spending had risen to roughly $25 billion — about $150 billion in today's dollars — driven by the accelerated timeline of the space race against the Soviet Union.

examples.hanzi: 我们的预算不够买新车。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de yùsuàn bú gòu mǎi xīn chē.
examples.english: Our budget isn't enough to buy a new car.

examples.hanzi: 装修之前最好先做个预算。
examples.pinyin: Zhuāngxiū zhīqián zuìhǎo xiān zuò ge yùsuàn.
examples.english: It's best to make a budget before renovating.

components.note: 犬 (dog) — animals: 狗, 猫; 状 first meant the shape of an animal.
丬 (a form of 爿) gives zhuàng: also in 壮 zhuàng, 装 zhuāng, 将 jiāng and 奖 jiǎng.

example.hanzi: 他现在的状态很好。
example.pinyin: Tā xiànzài de zhuàngtài hěn hǎo.
example.english: He is in great form right now.
example.fact: 状 covers appearance and condition (状态, 现状, 症状 symptoms) but also a document: 奖状 (certificate of merit), 告状 (to tattle or file a complaint). 状元 was the top scorer in the old imperial exams.

examples.hanzi: 医生问了问病人的情况和症状。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng wèn le wèn bìngrén de qíngkuàng hé zhèngzhuàng.
examples.english: The doctor asked about the patient's condition and symptoms.

examples.hanzi: 这个杯子的形状很特别。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bēizi de xíngzhuàng hěn tèbié.
examples.english: The shape of this cup is very unusual.

components.note: 木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; the fruit hangs on the tree.
田 (field) here is the round fruit drawn on the tree. 果 also gives the sound for 课 kè and 颗 kē.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.hanzi: 我猜他会迟到,果然他晚了半小时。
example.pinyin: Wǒ cāi tā huì chídào, guǒrán tā wǎn le bàn xiǎoshí.
example.english: I guessed he'd be late, and sure enough he was half an hour behind.
example.fact: Weather forecasters' predictions for tomorrow are correct roughly 80-90% of the time in most regions, but accuracy drops steeply beyond about a week because the atmosphere is a chaotic system — tiny, unmeasurable differences in starting conditions can snowball into completely different outcomes, a phenomenon known as the butterfly effect.

examples.hanzi: 天气预报说会下雨，果然下了。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì yùbào shuō huì xiàyǔ, guǒrán xià le.
examples.english: The forecast said it would rain, and sure enough it did.

examples.hanzi: 你果然没有骗我。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ guǒrán méiyǒu piàn wǒ.
examples.english: As expected, you didn't lie to me.

components.note: 钅 (metal, from 金) — marks metals, as in 铁, 钱, 银; 锁 is a metal lock. The right side matches 琐 suǒ and 唢 suǒ.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 手机屏幕已经锁定,需要输入密码。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī píngmù yǐjīng suǒdìng, xūyào shūrù mìmǎ.
example.english: The phone screen is locked and requires a password to unlock.
example.fact: Modern smartphone fingerprint sensors don't store an actual image of your fingerprint at all — they convert the ridge pattern into a mathematical template and keep it in an isolated secure enclave chip, so even if a phone's main storage is compromised, the fingerprint data itself typically can't be reconstructed from it.

examples.hanzi: 请把你的账户锁定，以免被盗。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de zhànghù suǒdìng, yǐmiǎn bèi dào.
examples.english: Please lock your account to keep it from being stolen.

examples.hanzi: 警察已经锁定了嫌疑人的位置。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá yǐjīng suǒdìng le xiányírén de wèizhi.
examples.english: The police have locked on to the suspect's location.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — boundaries and surroundings: 国 country, 园 garden, 回 return; 图 is a drawn plan of a region.
片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).

example.hanzi: 他在网上发了几张旅行的图片。
example.pinyin: Tā zài wǎngshàng fā le jǐ zhāng lǚxíng de túpiàn.
example.english: He posted a few pictures of his trip online.
example.fact: The first permanent photograph, taken by Joseph Nicéphore Niépce in 1826 or 1827, required an exposure time of roughly eight hours, capturing sunlight moving across a courtyard so that shadows appear on both sides of buildings in the same shot — a giveaway that the sun had crossed most of the sky during the exposure.

examples.hanzi: 这张图片是在哪儿拍的？
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng túpiàn shì zài nǎr pāi de?
examples.english: Where was this picture taken?

examples.hanzi: 请上传一张清晰的图片。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng shàngchuán yì zhāng qīngxī de túpiàn.
examples.english: Please upload a clear picture.

components.note: 首 (head, first) — a picture of a head with hair on top, which became the word for first and chief: 首先, 元首, also a measure for songs.
巾 (cloth) — marks cloth and coverings, as in 布, 帽, 带, 帮; 席 is a woven mat, then a seat or place at a table.

example.hanzi: 她是这家公司的首席设计师。
example.pinyin: Tā shì zhè jiā gōngsī de shǒuxí shèjìshī.
example.english: She is the company's chief designer.
example.fact: The title 'Chief Executive Officer' only became common in the United States in the 1960s and 70s; before that, companies more often used titles like 'President' or 'General Manager,' and the modern C-suite naming pattern (CFO, COO, CTO) spread largely because it gave a clear, comparable hierarchy for investors and boards.

examples.hanzi: 首席执行官在会上发了言。
examples.pinyin: Shǒuxí zhíxíngguān zài huì shàng fā le yán.
examples.english: The chief executive spoke at the meeting.

examples.hanzi: 他担任乐团的首席小提琴手。
examples.pinyin: Tā dānrèn yuètuán de shǒuxí xiǎotíqín shǒu.
examples.english: He serves as the orchestra's principal violinist.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
巾 (cloth) — 巾 is a cloth radical, as in 帽 hat, 带 belt; 布 is cloth, and by extension to spread or announce, as in 宣布.

example.hanzi: 政府将在下周公布新的政策。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jiāng zài xià zhōu gōngbù xīn de zhèngcè.
example.english: The government will announce a new policy next week.
example.fact: Ancient Rome's Twelve Tables of law, drafted around 450 BC, were literally posted in the Forum on bronze or wooden tablets so that ordinary citizens could see the laws for themselves — one of the earliest known examples of a government publicly codifying and displaying its legal rules rather than leaving them to the memory of elite judges.

examples.hanzi: 比赛成绩将在明天公布。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài chéngjì jiāng zài míngtiān gōngbù.
examples.english: The match results will be announced tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 老师还没有公布考试的日期。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī hái méiyǒu gōngbù kǎoshì de rìqī.
examples.english: The teacher hasn't announced the exam date yet.

components.note: 心 (heart) — worry and suffering weigh on the heart; also in 想 think, 急 anxious.
串 (chuàn) rhymes with huàn but is only a loose sound clue.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 医院里的患者正在等待医生。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn lǐ de huànzhě zhèngzài děngdài yīshēng.
example.english: The patients in the hospital are waiting for the doctor.
example.fact: The placebo effect is strong enough that in clinical drug trials, patients given an inert sugar pill often report measurable improvement in symptoms like pain or nausea, simply from believing they received real medicine — which is why new drugs must beat a placebo, not just outperform doing nothing, to be approved.

examples.hanzi: 这位患者需要住院观察。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi huànzhě xūyào zhùyuàn guānchá.
examples.english: This patient needs to stay in the hospital for observation.

examples.hanzi: 医生耐心地给患者解释病情。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng nàixīn de gěi huànzhě jiěshì bìngqíng.
examples.english: The doctor patiently explained the condition to the patient.

meanings: the remaining years of one's life

components.note: 人 (person) — the roof-like top. 余 absorbed 餘 (food left over); the shape no longer explains 'remainder'. Memory aid: a person with leftovers.
食 (food) — the old 餘 had the food part 饣; 余 is its sound part (yú), the same series as 除 chú, 徐 xú, 途 tú, with loose matches.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 他决定余生都住在这个小村子里。
example.pinyin: Tā juédìng yúshēng dōu zhù zài zhège xiǎo cūnzi lǐ.
example.english: He decided to spend the rest of his life living in this small village.
example.fact: Jane Goodall began observing wild chimpanzees at Tanzania's Gombe Stream in 1960 and continued studying and advocating for them for the rest of her life, spanning over six decades — her early discovery that chimps use and make tools overturned the belief that tool use was a uniquely human trait.

examples.hanzi: 我希望余生都能和你在一起。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng yúshēng dōu néng hé nǐ zài yìqǐ.
examples.english: I hope to spend the rest of my life with you.

examples.hanzi: 他把余生都献给了教育事业。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ yúshēng dōu xiàn gěi le jiàoyù shìyè.
examples.english: He devoted the rest of his life to education.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike; 攴) — hitting actions, as in 收 gather, 教 teach, 改 change.
高 (gāo) is a loose sound clue for qiāo; it also appears in 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.
门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.hanzi: 有人在敲门,你能去开一下吗?
example.pinyin: Yǒurén zài qiāomén, nǐ néng qù kāi yīxià ma?
example.english: Someone is knocking on the door, can you go open it?
example.fact: Woodpeckers can strike a tree trunk up to 20 times per second, and their skulls have evolved a spongy layer of bone plus a tongue that wraps around the back of the skull to act as a cushioning strap — adaptations that keep the repeated impacts from causing brain injury.

examples.hanzi: 进来之前请先敲门。
examples.pinyin: Jìnlái zhīqián qǐng xiān qiāomén.
examples.english: Please knock on the door before coming in.

examples.hanzi: 他敲门敲了好几次，没人回答。
examples.pinyin: Tā qiāomén qiāo le hǎo jǐ cì, méi rén huídá.
examples.english: He knocked on the door several times, but nobody answered.

components.note: 斤 (axe) — chopping, as in 所, 斩: freshly cut wood is new (薪 xīn is firewood).
亲 (qīn) is a close sound clue for xīn.
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 我们打算在新年那天去看烟花。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎsuàn zài xīnnián nà tiān qù kàn yānhuā.
example.english: We plan to go watch fireworks on New Year's Day.
example.fact: January 1st was fixed as New Year's Day by the Romans in 46 BC when Julius Caesar introduced the Julian calendar, naming the month after Janus, the two-faced god who looked simultaneously into the past and the future — a fitting symbol for the turn of a year.

examples.hanzi: 新年快乐！祝你身体健康。
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián kuàilè! Zhù nǐ shēntǐ jiànkāng.
examples.english: Happy New Year! Wishing you good health.

examples.hanzi: 新年到了，家家户户都贴春联。
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián dào le, jiājiāhùhù dōu tiē chūnlián.
examples.english: The New Year has arrived, and every household puts up spring couplets.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the vertical stroke 丨 is the string being drawn back on a bow — 引 is to pull, then to attract and to cite.
发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).

example.hanzi: 这条新闻引发了社会的广泛讨论。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xīnwén yǐnfā le shèhuì de guǎngfàn tǎolùn.
example.english: This news triggered widespread discussion in society.
example.fact: The 2010 'flash crash' in US stock markets wiped out nearly a trillion dollars of value in about 36 minutes, triggered largely by high-frequency trading algorithms reacting to each other's rapid sell orders in a runaway feedback loop, before the market recovered most of its losses the same day.

examples.hanzi: 吃太多糖会引发很多健康问题。
examples.pinyin: Chī tài duō táng huì yǐnfā hěn duō jiànkāng wèntí.
examples.english: Eating too much sugar can cause many health problems.

examples.hanzi: 一句玩笑话引发了大家的笑声。
examples.pinyin: Yí jù wánxiào huà yǐnfā le dàjiā de xiàoshēng.
examples.english: A joke set off laughter from everyone.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) with 月 — the shady side of a hill, the opposite of 阳 (阝 with 日, sunny); yīn is the dark principle.
彡 (strokes of light or hair) — shining or decoration, as in 形 shape, 彩 colour, 须 beard.
景 (jǐng) is a close sound clue for yǐng; 景 itself meant light; 影 is its shadow.

example.hanzi: 那场事故给他留下了心理阴影。
example.pinyin: Nà chǎng shìgù gěi tā liúxià le xīnlǐ yīnyǐng.
example.english: That accident left a psychological shadow over him.
example.fact: A total solar eclipse's shadow, called the umbra, is typically only about 100-160 kilometers wide even though the Moon is 3,474 kilometers across, because the Moon must be almost exactly the same apparent size as the Sun in the sky — a coincidence that won't last forever, since the Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth.

examples.hanzi: 大树的阴影挡住了阳光。
examples.pinyin: Dà shù de yīnyǐng dǎngzhù le yángguāng.
examples.english: The shadow of the big tree blocked the sunlight.

examples.hanzi: 考试失败后，他走出了阴影。
examples.pinyin: Kǎoshì shībài hòu, tā zǒuchū le yīnyǐng.
examples.english: After failing the exam, he moved past the shadow it cast.

components.note: 彡 (strokes of light or hair) — shining or decoration, as in 形 shape, 彩 colour, 须 beard.
景 (jǐng) is a close sound clue for yǐng; 景 itself meant light; 影 is its shadow.
片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).

example.hanzi: 这部影片在国际电影节上获得了大奖。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù yǐngpiàn zài guójì diànyǐngjié shàng huòdé le dàjiǎng.
example.english: This film won a major award at the international film festival.
example.fact: The Cannes Film Festival was originally planned to launch in September 1939 as a response to fascist influence over the Venice Film Festival, but it was cancelled after just one day when Germany invaded Poland, and the festival didn't actually begin until 1946.

examples.hanzi: 周末我想去看一部新影片。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ xiǎng qù kàn yí bù xīn yǐngpiàn.
examples.english: This weekend I want to see a new film.

examples.hanzi: 这部影片讲的是一个家庭的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù yǐngpiàn jiǎng de shì yí ge jiātíng de gùshi.
examples.english: This film tells the story of a family.

components.note: 高 (tall) — a drawing of a tall tower building. 高 also sounds out 糕 gāo (cake), 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 他是下棋的高手,很少输。
example.pinyin: Tā shì xiàqí de gāoshǒu, hěn shǎo shū.
example.english: He's a chess expert and rarely loses.
example.fact: In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue became the first computer to beat a reigning world chess champion, Garry Kasparov, in a full match under tournament conditions — Kasparov later accused IBM of cheating, but analysis has generally attributed the loss to a buggy move by Deep Blue that Kasparov misread as a sign of superhuman insight, unsettling him for the rest of the match.

examples.hanzi: 他是我们公司的电脑高手。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen gōngsī de diànnǎo gāoshǒu.
examples.english: He is the computer expert at our company.

examples.hanzi: 民间有很多隐藏的高手。
examples.pinyin: Mínjiān yǒu hěn duō yǐncáng de gāoshǒu.
examples.english: There are many hidden masters among ordinary people.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.

example.hanzi: 这家店卖很多进口食品。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn mài hěn duō jìnkǒu shípǐn.
example.english: This store sells many imported food products.
example.fact: 品 appears in 商品, 产品, 食品 (food products), and 作品 (a work of art). As a verb it means to savor: 品茶, 品尝. 品 once also meant official rank, as in 九品 (nine grades).

examples.hanzi: 这家超市的商品很便宜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā chāoshì de shāngpǐn hěn piányi.
examples.english: The goods in this supermarket are very cheap.

examples.hanzi: 你可以品一品这杯茶。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ pǐn yi pǐn zhè bēi chá.
examples.english: You can savor this cup of tea.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — 疒 is the sickness radical, as in 病, 痛, 疼; 痕 is the scar a sore leaves.
艮 (gèn) — near sound — 痕 is hén; 艮 also sounds out 根 gēn and 很 hěn.

example.hanzi: 墙上留下了一些痕迹。
example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng liú xià le yìxiē hénjì.
example.english: Some marks were left on the wall.
example.fact: 痕 is mostly seen in compounds: 痕迹 (trace), 伤痕 (scar), 泪痕 (tear streaks), 裂痕 (crack). 裂痕 is also used figuratively for a rift in a relationship.

examples.hanzi: 她脸上还有一点泪痕。
examples.pinyin: Tā liǎn shàng hái yǒu yìdiǎn lèihén.
examples.english: There are still a few tear marks on her face.

examples.hanzi: 桌子上留下了一道划痕。
examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng liú xià le yí dào huáhén.
examples.english: A scratch was left on the table.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wood, as in 林, 树, 桥; a village among the trees.
寸 (cùn) hints at the sound: 村 cūn is close.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 这个村子里只有几十户人家。
example.pinyin: Zhège cūnzi lǐ zhǐyǒu jǐshí hù rénjiā.
example.english: There are only a few dozen households in this village.
example.fact: Hallstatt, a small Austrian village of fewer than 800 residents built on the edge of an alpine lake, has become so popular with tourists partly because a nearly identical full-scale replica was built in Boluo, China in 2012 — sparking a wave of visitors who wanted to see the real version.

examples.hanzi: 我爷爷出生在一个小村子里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye chūshēng zài yí ge xiǎo cūnzi lǐ.
examples.english: My grandfather was born in a small village.

examples.hanzi: 村子后面有一条清澈的小河。
examples.pinyin: Cūnzi hòumiàn yǒu yì tiáo qīngchè de xiǎohé.
examples.english: Behind the village there is a clear little stream.

components.note: 氵 (water) — nourishing moisture, as in 汤 soup, 河 river.
兹 (zī) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 磁 cí and 慈 cí.
口 (mouth) — tasting and speaking: 吃, 喝, 嗅; 味 is flavor.
未 (wèi) sounds exactly like 味; also 妹 mèi.

example.hanzi: 这道菜的滋味非常特别。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào cài de zīwèi fēicháng tèbié.
example.english: The flavor of this dish is very unique.
example.fact: Umami, the savory fifth basic taste alongside sweet, sour, salty, and bitter, was identified in 1908 by Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda, who traced it to glutamate in kombu seaweed broth — but it wasn't formally recognized by Western food science until dedicated umami taste receptors were confirmed on the tongue in the early 2000s.

examples.hanzi: 生活中有酸甜苦辣各种滋味。
examples.pinyin: Shēnghuó zhōng yǒu suān tián kǔ là gèzhǒng zīwèi.
examples.english: Life has all kinds of flavors, sour, sweet, bitter and spicy.

examples.hanzi: 离开家的滋味并不好受。
examples.pinyin: Líkāi jiā de zīwèi bìng bù hǎoshòu.
examples.english: Leaving home is not a pleasant feeling.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 导演用了一种独特的手法来讲这个故事。
example.pinyin: Dǎoyǎn yòng le yī zhǒng dútè de shǒufǎ lái jiǎng zhège gùshì.
example.english: The director used a unique technique to tell this story.
example.fact: Alfred Hitchcock pioneered a camera technique now called the 'dolly zoom,' where the camera physically moves backward while the lens zooms in at the same time, distorting perspective to create a disorienting, vertigo-like sensation — he used it in the 1958 film Vertigo to visualize the protagonist's fear of heights.

examples.hanzi: 这位老师的教学手法很灵活。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎoshī de jiàoxué shǒufǎ hěn línghuó.
examples.english: This teacher's teaching methods are very flexible.

examples.hanzi: 骗子用同样的手法骗了很多人。
examples.pinyin: Piànzi yòng tóngyàng de shǒufǎ piàn le hěn duō rén.
examples.english: The con artist used the same trick to fool many people.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 右 is a hand 又 plus 口 (mouth) — as a memory aid, the right hand brings food to the mouth; 右 also sounds out 佑 yòu.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 他用右手写字。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng yòushǒu xiězì.
example.english: He writes with his right hand.
example.fact: About 90% of people are right-handed, a ratio that has stayed remarkably stable across cultures and centuries, and researchers have traced evidence of this same left-brain dominance for tool use back to Homo habilis stone tools roughly 1.8 million years old, suggesting handedness has deep evolutionary roots tied to brain lateralization.

examples.hanzi: 请举起你的右手。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jǔqǐ nǐ de yòushǒu.
examples.english: Please raise your right hand.

examples.hanzi: 他的右手受伤了，不能写字。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yòushǒu shòushāng le, bù néng xiězì.
examples.english: His right hand is injured, so he can't write.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
氵 (water) — 洋 is the ocean, as in 海 sea, 河 river.
羊 (yáng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 样 yàng, 养 yǎng and 详 xiáng.

example.hanzi: 太平洋是世界上最大的海洋。
example.pinyin: Tàipíngyáng shì shìjiè shàng zuìdà de hǎiyáng.
example.english: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean in the world.
example.fact: The Pacific Ocean covers about 165 million square kilometers — larger than the combined landmass of every continent on Earth — and its deepest point, the Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep, plunges nearly 11,000 meters, deep enough to submerge Mount Everest with over a kilometer of ocean left above its peak.

examples.hanzi: 我想去海边看看辽阔的海洋。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù hǎibiān kànkan liáokuò de hǎiyáng.
examples.english: I'd like to go to the seaside and see the vast ocean.

examples.hanzi: 海洋里生活着很多神奇的动物。
examples.pinyin: Hǎiyáng lǐ shēnghuózhe hěn duō shénqí de dòngwù.
examples.english: Many amazing animals live in the ocean.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — weather radical, as in 雪 snow, 雷 thunder; with 隹 (bird) it pictures birds startled in a storm, hence suddenly.
隹 (short-tailed bird) — appears in bird characters like 难, 谁, 集.
化 (huà) — near sound — 华 is huá; 化 also changes tone to sound out 华.
十 (ten) — the bottom 十 is a simplified remnant; 华 is flowery and splendid, as in 中华.
彳 (step, conduct) — 彳 is a step or going, as in 行 and 往; 德 is conduct.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart — the old 悳 was a straight 直 heart, so upright inner conduct.

example.hanzi: 霍华德是我们公司新来的经理。
example.pinyin: Huòhuádé shì wǒmen gōngsī xīnlái de jīnglǐ.
example.english: Howard is the new manager who just joined our company.
example.fact: Howard Carter, the British archaeologist whose name shares its Chinese transliteration pattern with names like Howard, spent nearly a decade searching the Valley of the Kings before discovering the almost fully intact tomb of Tutankhamun in 1922 — one of the most significant archaeological finds of the 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 霍华德每天骑自行车上班。
examples.pinyin: Huòhuádé měi tiān qí zìxíngchē shàngbān.
examples.english: Howard rides a bike to work every day.

examples.hanzi: 你认识霍华德吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi Huòhuádé ma?
examples.english: Do you know Howard?

components.note: 友 (friend) replaces the heart-and-foot lower part of the traditional 愛, which had 心 (heart); so 爱 lost its heart in simplification.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 他的爱好是收集老照片。
example.pinyin: Tā de àihào shì shōují lǎo zhàopiàn.
example.english: His hobby is collecting old photographs.
example.fact: Philately, the hobby of stamp collecting, exploded in popularity within a few years of the first adhesive postage stamp, the Penny Black, being issued by Britain in 1840 — one rare example, the 1856 British Guiana One-Cent Magenta, later sold at auction for over $9 million, making it the most valuable stamp in the world.

examples.hanzi: 你有什么业余爱好？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme yèyú àihào?
examples.english: What hobbies do you have in your spare time?

examples.hanzi: 我爱好摄影，经常去郊外拍照。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ àihào shèyǐng, jīngcháng qù jiāowài pāizhào.
examples.english: I'm fond of photography and often go to the countryside to take photos.

components.note: 乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".
见 (see) — seeing and vision: 看, 现, 视, 览; 观 is to watch. 又 only stands in for the old sound part 雚 (guàn).

example.hanzi: 即使遇到困难,她也一直很乐观。
example.pinyin: Jíshǐ yùdào kùnnán, tā yě yīzhí hěn lèguān.
example.english: Even when facing difficulties, she always stays optimistic.
example.fact: The Nun Study, a long-running research project on a convent of Catholic nuns, found that sisters who wrote more positive, optimistic language in autobiographical essays as young adults in the 1930s and 40s lived on average about 10 years longer than those with less positive language, one of the strongest links found between outlook and longevity.

examples.hanzi: 他是个乐观的人，总是笑着面对问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge lèguān de rén, zǒngshì xiàozhe miànduì wèntí.
examples.english: He is an optimistic person who always faces problems with a smile.

examples.hanzi: 医生对她的恢复情况很乐观。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng duì tā de huīfù qíngkuàng hěn lèguān.
examples.english: The doctor is optimistic about her recovery.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) on the right, as in 到, 别, 利; 创 first meant a cut wound and then to create.
仓 (cāng) — near sound — 创 is chuàng; 仓 also sounds out 抢 qiǎng and 枪 qiāng.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).

example.hanzi: 士兵在战场上留下了严重的创伤。
example.pinyin: Shìbīng zài zhànchǎng shàng liúxià le yánzhòng de chuāngshāng.
example.english: The soldier suffered a serious wound on the battlefield.
example.fact: During World War I, the introduction of steel helmets is estimated to have reduced fatal head wounds among soldiers by as much as 75%, prompting armies across Europe to rapidly replace cloth and leather caps — a shift driven directly by battlefield medical data on the most common causes of death.

examples.hanzi: 这次意外给孩子带来了心理创伤。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì yìwài gěi háizi dàilái le xīnlǐ chuāngshāng.
examples.english: The accident left the child with psychological trauma.

examples.hanzi: 医生正在处理他腿上的创伤。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng zhèngzài chǔlǐ tā tuǐ shàng de chuāngshāng.
examples.english: The doctor is treating the wound on his leg.

components.note: 至 (arrive) — oldest form is an arrow landing on a mark: to reach. 至 sounds out 到 dào and 致 zhì, and sits in 室 shì room and 屋 wū.
今 (now, today) — gives sound to 琴 qín, 含 hán, 念 niàn and 吟 yín; the old picture is uncertain.

example.hanzi: 这个问题至今没有得到解决。
example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí zhìjīn méiyǒu dédào jiějué.
example.english: This problem still hasn't been resolved to this day.
example.fact: The Voynich Manuscript, a roughly 240-page handwritten book filled with an unknown script and bizarre illustrations of plants and astrological symbols, has resisted every attempt at decipherment since it resurfaced in 1912 — carbon dating places the vellum to the early 1400s, but no one has confirmed to this day whether it encodes a real language, a cipher, or an elaborate hoax.

examples.hanzi: 我们至今还保持着联系。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhìjīn hái bǎochí zhe liánxì.
examples.english: We still keep in touch to this day.

examples.hanzi: 至今为止，他一次也没迟到过。
examples.pinyin: Zhìjīn wéizhǐ, tā yí cì yě méi chídào guo.
examples.english: So far, he has never once been late.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — marks the head and face, as in 顶, 题, 顺; 预 is thinking ahead.
予 (yǔ) hints at the sound: 预 yù is close, as in 豫 yù.
田 (field) — the bottom part. 备 is simplified from 備; the dictionary story is a trip to the 田 field to prepare for harvest. Treat it as a memory aid.
夂 (going down, slow step) — the top. Memory aid: heading 夂 to the field 田 to get ready — 准备, 设备.

example.hanzi: 运动员正在预备明天的比赛。
example.pinyin: Yùndòngyuán zhèngzài yùbèi míngtiān de bǐsài.
example.english: The athletes are preparing for tomorrow's competition.
example.fact: Olympic gymnasts often train for six to eight hours a day, six days a week, for years before a single competition, and elite programs like those in Romania and China have historically started identifying and training prospective gymnasts as young as five or six years old, decades before an athlete might reach the Olympic stage.

examples.hanzi: 请大家预备好笔和纸。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā yùbèi hǎo bǐ hé zhǐ.
examples.english: Everyone, please get your pens and paper ready.

examples.hanzi: 晚饭已经预备好了。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnfàn yǐjīng yùbèi hǎo le.
examples.english: Dinner is already prepared.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 损 is to damage, as in 损失.
员 (yuán) — loose hint — 损 is sǔn.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).

example.hanzi: 长时间用眼会损伤视力。
example.pinyin: Cháng shíjiān yòngyǎn huì sǔnshāng shìlì.
example.english: Using your eyes for a long time can damage your eyesight.
example.fact: Prolonged exposure to loud noise above about 85 decibels — roughly the volume of heavy city traffic — can permanently damage the tiny hair cells in the inner ear that convert sound vibrations into nerve signals, and unlike many other cells in the human body, these hair cells do not regenerate once destroyed.

examples.hanzi: 吸烟会损伤肺部。
examples.pinyin: Xīyān huì sǔnshāng fèibù.
examples.english: Smoking damages the lungs.

examples.hanzi: 这次摔倒没有损伤他的骨头。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shuāidǎo méiyǒu sǔnshāng tā de gǔtou.
examples.english: This fall didn't injure his bones.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
敝 (bì) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 蔽 bì (to cover), as in 作弊 to cheat.

example.hanzi: 考试作弊会受到严重的处罚。
example.pinyin: Kǎoshì zuòbì huì shòudào yánzhòng de chǔfá.
example.english: Cheating on an exam will result in serious punishment.
example.fact: In imperial China's civil service examinations, which could last up to three days and determined access to government office, some candidates smuggled in cheat sheets sewn into the lining of their clothing — surviving examples show thousands of tiny handwritten characters covering entire silk undergarments, some now preserved in museums.

examples.hanzi: 学生考试时不能作弊。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshēng kǎoshì shí bù néng zuòbì.
examples.english: Students must not cheat during exams.

examples.hanzi: 他因为作弊被老师发现了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi zuòbì bèi lǎoshī fāxiàn le.
examples.english: He was caught cheating by the teacher.

components.note: 氵 (water) — a stream to cross; also in 河 river, 游 swim.
步 (step) — steps through water: wading, hence being involved in something.
及 (reach) — a hand 又 catching up with a person from behind: to reach, then and; seen in 以及, 及时.

example.hanzi: 这个案子涉及多个国家的公司。
example.pinyin: Zhège ànzi shèjí duō gè guójiā de gōngsī.
example.english: This case involves companies from multiple countries.
example.fact: The 2015 Volkswagen emissions scandal involved software installed in roughly 11 million diesel vehicles worldwide that could detect when a car was undergoing an emissions test and temporarily reduce pollution output, only to revert to much higher, illegal emission levels during ordinary driving.

examples.hanzi: 这份报告涉及很多专业知识。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàogào shèjí hěn duō zhuānyè zhīshi.
examples.english: This report involves a lot of specialized knowledge.

examples.hanzi: 我不想涉及私人问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng shèjí sīrén wèntí.
examples.english: I don't want to touch on personal matters.

components.note: 彳 (step, 双人旁) — walking and journeys, as in 行 go, 往 toward, 得; 征 is a march or campaign.
正 (zhèng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 证 zhèng, 政 zhèng and 整 zhěng.
月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.

example.hanzi: 登山者最终征服了这座高峰。
example.pinyin: Dēngshānzhě zuìzhōng zhēngfú le zhè zuò gāofēng.
example.english: The climber finally conquered this high peak.
example.fact: Mount Everest was first confirmed climbed to its summit in 1953 by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, but the mountain still claims lives nearly every climbing season — the 'death zone' above 8,000 meters has so little oxygen that human bodies begin dying cell by cell even while resting, which is why speed and weather timing are critical to survival.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影征服了全世界的观众。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng zhēngfú le quán shìjiè de guānzhòng.
examples.english: This movie won over audiences around the world.

examples.hanzi: 他想用实力征服评委。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng yòng shílì zhēngfú píngwěi.
examples.english: He wants to win over the judges with his ability.

components.note: 木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; the fruit hangs on the tree.
田 (field) here is the round fruit drawn on the tree. 果 also gives the sound for 课 kè and 颗 kē.

example.hanzi: 我最喜欢吃的水果是苹果。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan chī de shuǐguǒ shì píngguǒ.
example.english: My favourite fruit is the apple.
example.fact: 果 is a fruit on a tree, and fruit became the metaphor for results: 结果 (result), 效果 (effect), 因果 (cause and effect), 果然 (as expected). In fruit names it often follows the type: 苹果, 水果.

examples.hanzi: 这个果子又大又甜。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guǒzi yòu dà yòu tián.
examples.english: This fruit is big and sweet.

examples.hanzi: 他没有努力学习，结果考试没通过。
examples.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu nǔlì xuéxí, jiéguǒ kǎoshì méi tōngguò.
examples.english: He did not study hard, so as a result he failed the exam.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
尸 (roof, body) — 尸 acts as a roof or shelter here, as in 居 and 层; 屋 is a covered place.
至 (arrive) — 至 is where one arrives, so 屋 is a place you get to and stay — a room or house.

example.hanzi: 他们在山上盖了一间小屋。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài shānshàng gài le yī jiān xiǎowū.
example.english: They built a small cabin on the mountain.
example.fact: Henry David Thoreau's famous cabin at Walden Pond, the setting for his 1854 book Walden, measured only about 10 by 15 feet — roughly the size of a modern one-car garage — and he built most of it himself for around $28, a deliberate experiment in simple living close to nature.

examples.hanzi: 河边有一间白色的小屋。
examples.pinyin: Hébiān yǒu yì jiān báisè de xiǎowū.
examples.english: There is a little white cabin by the river.

examples.hanzi: 我们在山上的小屋里过了一夜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài shān shàng de xiǎowū lǐ guò le yí yè.
examples.english: We spent a night in a small cabin on the mountain.

components.note: 罒 (net) — 罒 is a net, as in 罚, 置; 罗 is a net, and is mostly seen in 罗马 Rome.
木 (tree) — 杰 is simplified from 傑; a tall tree makes a handy picture for an outstanding person standing tall.

example.hanzi: 罗杰是我大学时最好的朋友。
example.pinyin: Luójié shì wǒ dàxué shí zuìhǎo de péngyǒu.
example.english: Roger was my best friend during college.
example.fact: Roger Bannister became the first person to run a mile in under four minutes in 1954, clocking 3:59.4 — a barrier many physiologists at the time believed was beyond human capability — and remarkably, another runner broke his new record just 46 days later, showing how much of the limit had been psychological.

examples.hanzi: 罗杰明天要来我们家吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Luójié míngtiān yào lái wǒmen jiā chīfàn.
examples.english: Roger is coming to our house for dinner tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 这是罗杰送给我的书。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì Luójié sòng gěi wǒ de shū.
examples.english: This is a book Roger gave me.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 拿, 提, 抬; 搬 is to move things.
般 (bān) gives the sound exactly: 搬 bān.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.

example.hanzi: 他们下个月要搬进新房子。
example.pinyin: Tāmen xià gè yuè yào bānjìn xīn fángzi.
example.english: They are moving into a new house next month.
example.fact: The Biosphere 2 project in Arizona sealed eight scientists inside a giant glass and steel enclosure for two years starting in 1991, growing their own food and recycling their own air and water, in an experiment meant to test whether humans could live self-sufficiently — a scaled-up rehearsal for one day moving into a habitat on Mars.

examples.hanzi: 我们刚搬进新家，还没整理好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gāng bānjìn xīn jiā, hái méi zhěnglǐ hǎo.
examples.english: We just moved into our new home and haven't unpacked yet.

examples.hanzi: 新同事已经搬进了隔壁的办公室。
examples.pinyin: Xīn tóngshì yǐjīng bānjìn le gébì de bàngōngshì.
examples.english: The new colleague has moved into the office next door.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".
罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and entrapment: 罗 net, 罚 punish, 骂 scold; here a net of wrongdoing 非 catching the guilty.
非 (not, wrong) — what is wrong or unlawful; in 罪 it is the wrongdoing caught in the net.

example.hanzi: 被告最终在法庭上认罪了。
example.pinyin: Bèigào zuìzhōng zài fǎtíng shàng rènzuì le.
example.english: The defendant finally pleaded guilty in court.
example.fact: Plea bargaining, where a defendant pleads guilty in exchange for a reduced sentence, resolves roughly 90-95% of criminal cases in the United States without ever going to trial, a proportion so high that some legal scholars argue the modern American justice system functions primarily as a system of negotiated pleas rather than trials by jury.

examples.hanzi: 他在警察面前认罪了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jǐngchá miànqián rènzuì le.
examples.english: He pleaded guilty in front of the police.

examples.hanzi: 只有认罪，才能得到宽大处理。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu rènzuì, cáinéng dédào kuāndà chǔlǐ.
examples.english: Only by admitting guilt can one receive leniency.

components.note: 又 (hand) — two hands 又 stacked: hands joined in friendship.
羊 (sheep) — 羊 is a symbol of good fortune, as in 美 and 祥; 善 is goodness and kindness, together with 口 (words).

example.hanzi: 当地居民对游客都很友善。
example.pinyin: Dāngdì jūmín duì yóukè dōu hěn yǒushàn.
example.english: The local residents are all very friendly to tourists.
example.fact: Bonobos, close genetic relatives of chimpanzees, are notably less aggressive toward strangers and more prone to sharing food with unfamiliar individuals than chimps are, a difference researchers link partly to bonobo societies being led by females and to lower competition for food in their central African habitat.

examples.hanzi: 邻居们对新搬来的人很友善。
examples.pinyin: Línjūmen duì xīn bān lái de rén hěn yǒushàn.
examples.english: The neighbors are very friendly to the newcomers.

examples.hanzi: 他友善地向我们挥了挥手。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒushàn de xiàng wǒmen huī le huī shǒu.
examples.english: He waved to us in a friendly way.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — marks grain and crops, as in 秋, 种, 租; 称 originally meant weighing grain, then naming (称呼).
之 (of, go) — oldest form is a foot leaving a starting line: "to go". Now it is a literary particle meaning "of" or "it".
力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.

example.hanzi: 人们称之为世界第八大奇迹。
example.pinyin: Rénmen chēngzhīwéi shìjiè dì bā dà qíjì.
example.english: People call it the eighth wonder of the world.
example.fact: The original Seven Wonders of the Ancient World were first listed by Greek writers around the 2nd century BC, but only one of them, the Great Pyramid of Giza, still survives today — the other six, including the Hanging Gardens of Babylon and the Colossus of Rhodes, were destroyed by earthquakes, fire, or war over the centuries.

examples.hanzi: 人们称之为“春运”。
examples.pinyin: Rénmen chēng zhī wéi “chūnyùn”.
examples.english: People call it the “spring travel rush”.

examples.hanzi: 这种现象，科学家称之为全球变暖。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng xiànxiàng, kēxuéjiā chēng zhī wéi quánqiú biànnuǎn.
examples.english: Scientists call this phenomenon global warming.
